newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher on thin volumes.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher on thin volumes.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher after gaining early in a light-volume rally tied to an influx of commercial buying, traders said.
Traders said strong buy orders at the opening caused local traders to cover the short positions they had assumed at the session's close on Monday.
Spring wheat then coasted to end higher on a lack of selling and spillover support from Chicago and Kansas City.
"This is just a real light-volume affair. We've seen some commercial buying and not a lot of selling above the market," an MGE floor source said at midsession.
MGE spring wheat closed unchanged to 4-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-3/4 cents at $3.79. Dec gained 4-1/4 cents to close at $4.21-3/4.
Despite Tuesday's firm close, there was still widespread concern that U.S. wheat is priced too high to let it compete effectively with wheat from other exporting countries.

Traders said Atwood/Peavey bought 800,000 March. Benson-Quinn and Country Hedging each sold at least 500,000 March. LFG bought around 1.8 million Minneapolis March on the intermarket spread with Chicago. Atwood/Peavey bull-spread 450,000 March/Dec at 41 to 43 cents per bushel.
MGE barley closed 1/2 to five cents per cwt higher, with March up 1/2 cent at $6.54-1/2.
